target: Il ne tient qu'à vous de changer les choses.
english: It's up to you to change things.
tip: Tenir usually means 'to hold,' but 'il ne tient qu'à vous' means 'it rests entirely on you.' The ne...qu' narrows it to 'only you' – it's up to you alone.
'À bon chat, bon rat' is literally 'to a good cat, a good rat' – a sharp attacker meets an equally sharp defender. Evenly matched.
Aucun normally means 'none', but d'aucuns flips it: an old plural for 'some people'. D'aucuns diront = some will say.
'Errare humanum est' is Latin – 'to err is human' – dropped whole into formal French. It often continues: perseverare diabolicum (to persist, diabolical).

target: Vaille que vaille, il a terminé le travail.
english: Come what may, he finished the work.
tip: Vaille is the subjunctive of valoir (to be worth), frozen twice: vaille que vaille literally 'be it worth what it may' = come what may.

target: Toujours est-il que la décision a été prise.
english: The fact remains that the decision has been made.
tip: Est-il here isn't a question – French inverts the verb after certain set openers. Toujours est-il que = the fact remains that.

target: C'est à se demander si cela en vaut la peine.
english: It makes you wonder if it's worth it.
tip: 'C'est à' + infinitive: 'c'est à se demander' = it makes you wonder. Impersonal consequence expression.
